investor.question: What is the legal structure?
investor.answer: Amora uses a Horizontal Condominium under Costa Rican law, combined with a 508(c)(1)(a) community organization. Individual lot ownership with shared commons management.

investor.question: How does debt vs equity work?
investor.answer: We prefer debt financing to keep community ownership intact. Investors lend to the project and receive interest plus priority on lot purchases.

investor.question: What is the minimum investment?
investor.answer: Minimum amounts vary by vehicle. Contact the team to discuss options that match your capacity.

investor.question: What are my exit options?
investor.answer: Investors can exit through lot sale at appreciated value, business equity stake, or structured buy-back options. We prioritize liquidity for investors who need it.

investor.question: What if the project doesn't complete?
investor.answer: Investors hold debt secured against the land. In the unlikely event of project failure, debt holders have first claim on the 266-acre property which was appraised at $16M+ in January 2026.

investor.question: Can I live at Amora as an investor?
investor.answer: Yes. Investors who become residents get priority access to lots, and you can build a home on your lot. Your investment can apply toward your Land Share Agreement.

investor.question: What fees are involved?
investor.answer: Annual village contribution fee covers shared services, infrastructure maintenance, and circle operations. Exact amounts will be detailed in your investor pack.

investor.question: How does governance work?
investor.answer: Resident investors gain voice in village decisions through our consent-based circle system. The more you contribute over time, the more governance weight you earn.

investor.question: When is ROI expected?
investor.answer: The 15-year financial model projects returns from resort, retail, and residential components. Year-by-year projections are in the Investor Pack.

steward.question: How are decisions made?
steward.answer: Through sociocratic circles using consent-based decision making. No single person, including the founders, can override a community consent vote.

steward.question: Do I get paid as a Village Steward?
steward.answer: Contributions are recognised in Gratitude, the village's signal of appreciation. Gratitude carries no financial value on its own. Each cycle the community shares a real pool of value tokens across everyone's Gratitude, and as Amora's shared businesses generate revenue those tokens can convert to cash, equity, or community currency.

steward.question: How much time does stewardship require?
steward.answer: Roles are seasonal (3-month commitments). The time varies by role: some are a few hours per week, others are near full-time.

resident.question: What internet is available?
resident.answer: Dominicalito has reliable fiber internet. The village will have dedicated high-speed connection for residents and home offices.

resident.question: What schooling options exist for children?
resident.answer: Plans include an on-site learning center. Local bilingual schools are within 20 minutes. Many resident families are worldschoolers.

resident.question: Can I own my home outright?
resident.answer: Land Share Agreements provide long-term secure access, renewable and inheritable by your children tax-free. The community co-owns the land, you own your structure.

prosperity.question: What businesses are needed?
prosperity.answer: The Prosperity Packet details all opportunities. High-priority needs include food production, wellness services, childcare, construction, and technology.

prosperity.question: How does revenue sharing work?
prosperity.answer: A percentage of revenue (exact structure in the Prosperity Packet) flows back to the village community. Contributions are acknowledged in Gratitude, and value reaches members through the cycle pool of value tokens. You operate your business; the community benefits from your success.

prosperity.question: Do I need to live at Amora to run a business?
prosperity.answer: Some businesses require on-site presence. Others can be managed remotely. Discuss your model with the team during your Prosperity Call.

visitConfig.hero_subtitle: Experience the land, meet the people, and decide if Amora is where you belong.

visit_types.title: Community Call
visit_types.description: Meet the founding team and current members. Ask any question. Hear the vision directly. This is your first step.

visit_types.title: Land Tour Visit
visit_types.description: Walk the 266 acres with a founding team member. See the infrastructure underway. Stay nearby or camp on the land. Meals with the community included.

visit_types.title: Village Weaving Immersion
visit_types.description: Live and work alongside the founding community. Shadow circle meetings, contribute to active projects, and discover where your gifts are most needed. This is the deepest way to know before you commit.

logistics.getting_there: Dominicalito is on Costa Rica's Pacific coast. Nearest airport: Quepos (45 min) or San Jose (3.5 hours). Charter flights available to Quepos from the US west coast.
logistics.accommodation: Accommodation details will be provided when you book. Options range from nearby guesthouses to on-land camping.
logistics.what_to_bring: Comfortable outdoor clothes, sun protection, rain gear. The dry season runs December to April; green season May to November brings afternoon rain.
logistics.contact_note: Ready to visit? Fill in the form below or email the team directly.
